symptom_terms.zh-CN: 受压或缺氧环境后呼吸困难、意识改变
symptom_terms.en: breathing difficulty or altered awareness after compression or oxygen-depleted exposure

text.zh-CN:
窒息是身体不能获得足够氧气的危险状态，本页重点讲机械性和环境性窒息。

- 口鼻被覆盖会挡住空气；颈部受压还可阻断脑部血流；胸部被压住则可能无法有效扩张。
- 食物或异物卡喉、一氧化碳中毒、肺部ARDS及新生儿呼吸窘迫有各自处理路径，不能全部归为本页的同一病因。
text.en:
Asphyxiation means inadequate oxygen reaching the body; this page focuses on mechanical and environmental causes.

- Covering the mouth and nose blocks air, neck compression can also interrupt blood flow to the brain, and chest compression can prevent effective expansion.
- Food or foreign-body choking, carbon-monoxide poisoning, ARDS and newborn respiratory distress have separate pathways rather than one shared cause.

text.zh-CN:
发生方式决定救援方法；首先弄清是否仍有外部危险。

- 袋子或软物覆盖口鼻、绳带勒颈、胸部受压或被困于限制呼吸的姿势，都可能使人缺氧。
- 储罐、坑井和其他密闭空间可能缺氧或有毒气体；不能凭没有气味、看起来空旷就判断安全。
- 颈部受压可能没有明显伤痕，不能用皮肤完好排除内部损伤；暴力、事故和自伤均需了解具体经过。
text.en:
The mechanism determines rescue: first identify any ongoing external danger.

- Bags or soft objects over the face, ligatures around the neck, chest compression or positions that restrict breathing can deprive a person of oxygen.
- Tanks, pits and other confined spaces may lack oxygen or contain toxic gases; appearance or lack of smell does not establish safety.
- Neck compression may leave no obvious marks. Intact skin does not exclude internal injury; the circumstances of assault, accident or self-harm matter.

text.zh-CN:
呼吸困难、不能正常回应或倒地不动，需要立即呼叫当地急救服务。

- 没有反应且没有正常呼吸，或只有断续喘息，按可能心脏骤停处理；普通旁观者不要因尝试摸脉搏而耽误复苏。
- 勒颈后声音变哑、吞咽困难、颈部肿痛、昏厥、混乱、抽搐或一侧肢体无力，都需紧急评估，即使已松开压迫。
text.en:
Difficulty breathing, reduced responsiveness or collapse requires immediate contact with local emergency services.

- Treat unresponsiveness with absent or abnormal breathing, including gasping, as possible cardiac arrest; lay rescuers should not delay resuscitation to check a pulse.
- After neck compression, hoarseness, difficult swallowing, neck swelling or pain, fainting, confusion, seizures or one-sided weakness need emergency assessment even after pressure is released.

text.zh-CN:
先保护救援者，再按调度员指导提供力所能及的帮助。

- 不要贸然进入疑似缺氧的坑井、储罐或密闭空间救人；呼叫专业救援并说明场所及危险，普通口罩不能替代专门呼吸防护。
- 现场安全且可直接解除时移开覆盖口鼻的物体；被重物困住或有持续危险时需要专业救援，不让更多人受伤。
- 无反应且不正常呼吸时开始胸外按压并取用AED，按调度员及设备提示操作；受训且愿意者加入人工呼吸，不能人工呼吸时持续按压。
- 仍正常呼吸但无反应者持续观察；按指导保持气道通畅。怀疑颈背损伤时避免不必要搬动，但气道和呼吸优先。
text.en:
Protect the rescuer first, then give assistance within your abilities under dispatcher guidance.

- Do not enter a potentially oxygen-depleted pit, tank or confined space for an improvised rescue. Tell professional responders the location and hazard; an ordinary mask cannot replace appropriate respiratory protection.
- Remove a face covering when the scene is safe and it is directly accessible. Entrapment under heavy objects or ongoing hazards requires professional rescue without exposing more people.
- For an unresponsive person not breathing normally, begin compressions and obtain an AED, following dispatcher and device instructions. Trained, willing rescuers add rescue breaths; provide continuous compressions if breaths cannot be given.
- Keep monitoring an unresponsive person who is breathing normally and maintain the airway as instructed. Avoid unnecessary movement with suspected neck or back injury, while prioritizing airway and breathing.

text.zh-CN:
急诊先保障呼吸循环，再查清缺氧原因和损伤，不等检查完成才救命。

- 医护会询问受压部位、持续经过、昏迷和既往病，并检查呼吸、血压、心电和意识；血氧读数只是其中一项。
- 勒颈后的喉部检查可寻找气道损伤；有血管或脑损伤疑虑时可选择CT血管造影等检查，不是每人都做同一套扫描。
- 外观正常或初次检查未见明显异常不能替代后续观察；出现新的呼吸、吞咽或神经症状需重新评估。
text.en:
Emergency assessment prioritizes breathing and circulation while identifying the cause and injury; lifesaving care does not wait for completed testing.

- Clinicians ask about the site and course of compression, loss of consciousness and previous illness, then assess breathing, blood pressure, cardiac rhythm and awareness; pulse oximetry is only one component.
- Laryngeal assessment after strangulation looks for airway injury; suspected vascular or brain injury may require CT angiography or other imaging rather than an identical scan package for everyone.
- Normal appearance or an initially reassuring examination does not replace monitoring; new breathing, swallowing or neurological symptoms require reassessment.

text.zh-CN:
“喘不过气”还可能来自气道疾病、中毒或心肺问题，需要区别原因。

- 进食时突然不能说话或有效咳嗽提示异物堵塞，应走年龄适用的卡喉急救路径；不要把所有窒息都做腹部冲击。
- 喘鸣伴过敏暴露可能是严重过敏反应；哮喘、肺水肿、气胸及药物过量也可造成呼吸困难或呼吸停止，治疗各不相同。
- 缺氧后的混乱可被误认为醉酒或精神问题；应说明受压或危险环境经过，不能仅凭行为表现排除损伤。
text.en:
Breathlessness can also arise from airway disease, poisoning or heart and lung problems; the cause must be distinguished.

- An abrupt inability to speak or cough effectively while eating suggests foreign-body obstruction and calls for an age-appropriate choking pathway; abdominal thrusts are not a treatment for every form of asphyxiation.
- Wheeze after an allergic exposure may be anaphylaxis. Asthma, pulmonary oedema, pneumothorax and overdose can also cause respiratory distress or arrest, with different treatments.
- Confusion after oxygen deprivation can resemble intoxication or a psychiatric problem; report the compression or hazardous exposure rather than excluding injury from behaviour alone.

text.zh-CN:
治疗目标是解除原因、恢复氧气进入及循环，并处理合并损伤。

- 医护可开放气道、清除阻塞、给氧，并在自主呼吸不足时辅助通气或插管；仅有氧气不等于已经有足够空气进出肺。
- 医护确认有脉搏却不能有效呼吸时，以通气支持并反复评估为重点；确认或疑似心脏骤停则进入CPR及AED流程，旁观者按无反应和异常呼吸判断。
- 勒颈后持续症状、检查异常或缺乏安全照护环境，可能需要留观或住院；已经醒来不等于所有风险解除。
text.en:
Treatment removes the cause, restores oxygen delivery and circulation, and addresses associated injury.

- Clinicians may open and clear the airway, give oxygen and assist ventilation or intubate when breathing is inadequate. Oxygen supply alone does not establish adequate movement of air through the lungs.
- When clinicians confirm a pulse but ineffective breathing, they prioritize ventilation and reassessment. Confirmed or suspected cardiac arrest follows CPR and AED pathways; lay rescuers use responsiveness and breathing.
- Persistent symptoms, abnormal findings or absence of safe support after strangulation may require observation or admission; awakening does not mean every risk has passed.

text.zh-CN:
窒息没有一粒通用的“解药”；药物取决于真正病因和损伤。

- 已知哮喘或严重过敏反应时，处方急救药有各自用途，但不能用吸入剂或抗过敏药替代解除机械压迫和恢复呼吸。
- 急救时把现用药、过敏史及可能接触的药物或化学品告诉团队；不要给无意识者喂药。
text.en:
There is no universal antidote pill for asphyxiation; medicines depend on the actual cause and injury.

- Prescribed rescue medicines have specific roles in known asthma or anaphylaxis, but inhalers or allergy medicines do not replace relief of mechanical compression and restoration of breathing.
- Tell responders about regular medicines, allergies and possible drug or chemical exposure; do not give oral medicines to an unconscious person.

text.zh-CN:
饮食不是恢复急性缺氧的治疗，能否吞咽取决于意识和气道状况。

- 没有反应、明显呼吸困难或吞咽受损时不要喂水、食物或口服药，以免进入气道；先接受急救及吞咽评估。
- 颈部损伤后出现吞咽痛或吞咽困难，应告诉医护，不能用强行喝水来试验是否已经恢复。
text.en:
Food is not treatment for acute oxygen deprivation; safe swallowing depends on consciousness and the airway.

- Do not give water, food or oral medicines when unresponsive, severely breathless or unable to swallow safely; obtain emergency care and swallowing assessment first.
- Report painful or difficult swallowing after neck injury rather than forcing drinks to test recovery.

text.zh-CN:
回家护理以出院指示和安全陪护为基础，不能用家庭观察替代应有的急诊评估。

- 勒颈或喉部损伤后按安排由可靠成人陪伴，了解新的呼吸、声音、吞咽或意识变化该如何求助。
- 受暴力或自伤影响者可在私密环境下向医护说明情况，讨论安全住所、心理和社会支持；不必在施害者面前解释。
text.en:
Home care follows discharge instructions and safe support; it does not replace indicated emergency assessment.

- After neck or throat injury, arrange reliable adult support as advised and know how to seek help for new breathing, voice, swallowing or awareness changes.
- People affected by violence or self-harm can speak privately with clinicians about safe accommodation and psychological or social support rather than explaining in front of an aggressor.

text.zh-CN:
儿童、孕妇及不能可靠描述经过的人，需要结合具体处境评估。

- 儿童疑似勒颈或虐待需要儿科及保护儿童团队参与；没有伤痕不能排除危险，不能直接套用成人出院决定。
- 孕妇受压或受伤时应告知孕周，团队同时考虑母体抢救和产科评估；检查选择由临床风险决定，不因怀孕自行拒绝必要急救。
- 婴儿意外口鼻覆盖的预防与出生时肺发育或表面活性物质问题不同；婴儿复苏应遵循年龄适用的调度指导和训练。
text.en:
Children, pregnant people and anyone unable to give a reliable history require assessment tailored to their circumstances.

- Suspected strangulation or abuse in a child requires paediatric and safeguarding involvement. Lack of marks does not exclude harm, and adult discharge decisions cannot simply be copied.
- Report gestational age after compression or injury in pregnancy. The team considers maternal resuscitation and obstetric assessment; clinical risk guides investigation rather than withholding necessary emergency care solely because of pregnancy.
- Preventing accidental covering of an infant’s face differs from treating lung immaturity or surfactant problems at birth; infant resuscitation follows age-appropriate dispatcher guidance and training.

text.zh-CN:
结果取决于缺氧程度、持续时间及伴随损伤，不能仅凭已清醒判断完全恢复。

- 按出院安排复诊；新出现呼吸困难、吞咽异常、昏厥、混乱、抽搐或肢体无力，应立即再次求助。
- 持续记忆、注意力或情绪变化应主动报告；可能需要脑损伤评估、康复或心理支持。
text.en:
Outcome depends on the severity and duration of oxygen deprivation and associated injury; being awake alone does not establish complete recovery.

- Attend arranged follow-up. New breathlessness, swallowing problems, fainting, confusion, seizures or weakness require immediate reassessment.
- Report persistent memory, concentration or mood changes; brain-injury assessment, rehabilitation or psychological support may be needed.

text.zh-CN:
缺氧可伤害大脑和其他重要器官，颈部损伤还有局部及血管并发症。

- 勒颈后的气道肿胀可延迟出现；血管损伤或血栓可能引起脑卒中，因此新的症状不能只当作普通淤青。
- 无意识者可能吸入呕吐物，导致新的气道或肺部问题；这也是急救时不喂东西、持续观察呼吸的原因。
text.en:
Oxygen deprivation can damage the brain and other vital organs; neck injury adds local and vascular complications.

- Airway swelling may develop after strangulation; vascular injury or clotting can cause stroke, so new symptoms should not be dismissed as an ordinary bruise.
- An unconscious person may inhale vomit, causing further airway or lung problems; this is one reason to avoid oral intake and keep monitoring breathing.

text.zh-CN:
预防应针对真实危险源：睡眠环境、颈部缠绕、受压场所和密闭空间。

- 婴儿每次睡眠仰卧，使用结实平坦的独立睡眠表面，床内不放枕头、松软被褥或玩具；不要在沙发或成人床上代替安全婴儿睡眠空间。
- 密闭空间作业要有受训人员、空气检测、通风、防护和救援方案；公众发现人员倒在其中时，先呼叫专业救援。
text.en:
Prevention targets the actual hazards: sleep environments, neck entanglement, compression and confined spaces.

- Place infants on their backs for every sleep on a firm, flat separate sleep surface without pillows, loose soft bedding or toys; a sofa or adult bed is not a substitute for a safe infant sleep space.
- Confined-space work requires trained staff, atmospheric testing, ventilation, protection and a rescue plan; members of the public finding someone collapsed inside should summon professional rescue first.

limitations.en: Original educational draft. Listed references await claim-level verification; no systematic review, independent dual-source confirmation or clinical sign-off is claimed.
